description: What if the key to exploring the Moon and Mars lies right here on Earth? 🌎🚀 Through research, scientific data analysis, and technology, our team developed TerraAnalog, a platform designed to identify and compare terrestrial environments that share characteristics with the Moon and Mars, helping pave the way for future space exploration missions.
summary:
Where on Earth could we prepare to explore another world? TerraAnalog is an interactive platform that connects eight terrestrial analog regions with lunar and Martian research objectives. Users navigate a 3D globe, explore separate Moon and Mars assessments, compare seven scientific categories, and access sixteen detailed reports.

Its “Find by Mission” feature ranks locations for investigations such as rover mobility, geology, water and ice, and subsurface exploration. Results explain contributing variables, data coverage, and limitations, helping users understand each comparison.

TerraAnalog combines compiled scientific references with NASA POWER climate context. Its similarity scores are preliminary AI-assisted assessments, while mission rankings follow an explicit, reproducible calculation.

Designed for students, educators, and preliminary research, TerraAnalog makes planetary comparisons accessible and connects terrestrial characteristics to exploration questions. Its central insight is simple: the most useful analog depends on the material, process, or experiment we want to investigate.
details:
TerraAnalog connects Earth’s environments with the questions that drive lunar and Martian exploration. Our interactive platform helps users investigate where terrestrial terrain, materials, and processes could support planetary research.

How it works

  • Explore Sites: Navigate a 3D globe featuring eight terrestrial analog regions, with geographic profiles, separate Moon and Mars assessments, and sixteen scientific reports.
  • Find by Mission: Compare locations for rover mobility, geology, water and resources, thermal testing, dust processes, subsurface exploration, and Martian astrobiology.

Assessments cover seven scientific categories, from topography and mineralogy to subsurface structures and habitability. Mission rankings use relevant variable scores and display contributing factors, data coverage, missing information, and limitations. Non-applicable variables are excluded; insufficient coverage is explicitly identified.

Data and methodology

The catalog combines compiled terrestrial research with lunar and Martian reference resources. NASA POWER provides separate climate context for representative coordinates. Similarity percentages are preliminary AI-assisted assessments; mission rankings apply a transparent, reproducible calculation to those stored scores. They support initial investigation rather than certify mission suitability.

Benefits and creativity

A location’s usefulness depends on the experiment. TerraAnalog makes specialized comparisons visible: a region may offer valuable geological materials despite limited overall environmental similarity. Students and educators can explore these connections, while researchers can use the catalog as a starting point for investigating field environments and testing opportunities.

Development

Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, globe.gl, and Three.js, the platform considers geographic scale, missing data, scientific applicability, and Earth’s environmental differences from other worlds. Detailed sources, explanations, and limitations remain available through its methodology page and reports.
